body.x: DNA Corporation, headed by CEO Ko Kyung-hwan, felt its presence at the ‘CES Unveiled’ global media event on January 7th, just before the official opening of CES 2024 in Las Vegas. Established in 2019 to provide a better life and a brighter future for children through AI-based DNA data utilization, DNA Corporation has proven its capabilities in AI-based diagnostic solutions. After two years of research, they launched ADHD BANK, a simple screening test for ADHD, which received a CES 2023 innovation award.

Expanding its adaptive range beyond child ADHD, DNA Corporation has now successfully developed OBST BANK (Obesity BANK). This genetic analysis kit, designed through research and exploring biomarkers in obese patients, aims to detect obesity early and provide personalized diagnoses.

OBST BANK is an AI-based DNA data solution that supports physicians in diagnosis and prediction. It utilizes a simple collection method of epithelial cells from infants at birth, which are then directly used for genetic analysis. This function facilitates research into obesity cases with genetic causes, like early childhood obesity.

Recognized for its exceptional functionality and distinction from other solutions, OBST BANK won the AI category innovation award at CES 2024. At CES Unveiled, it received promising evaluations from global attendees.

body.cap: Ko Kyung-hwan, DNA Corporation’s CEO, interacts with international media at CES Unveiled. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: CEO Ko Kyung-hwan commented, “Although this is only the second year DNA Corporation has participated in CES, I have experienced the atmosphere of the event for over a decade as a visitor. In particular, Unveiled provides an opportunity to showcase our technological prowess to global media across various categories, and I have long anticipated participating in this event. I am delighted that this aspiration has met the goal.”

He added, “As a company selected for innovation awards for two consecutive years at CES, DNA Corporation feels a unique sense of pride. We hope that our proven technological and competitive strengths will translate into tangible market influence, and we look forward to establishing close relationships with global media and influencers.”

The Consumer Technology Association (CTA), host of CES, the world’s largest IT exhibition, provides a platform in Las Vegas each January to showcase global consumer electronics trends. AVING News, covering CES for 18 consecutive years, has been reporting CES news worldwide since 2006, highlighting products, companies, and technologies with the ‘BEST OF CES’ and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA’ awards programs. They also discuss issues in the field from the CES scene through ‘AVING LIVE.’

The CES 2024 Seoul pavilion, operating on its most enormous scale since Seoul’s first CES participation in 2020, is a joint effort of 13 organizations, including SBA, Seoul Bio Hub, Campus Town, AI Yangjae Hub, Gwanak District, Yonsei University, Korea University, Chung-Ang University, Sogang University, Kookmin University, Hanyang University, Konkuk University, and Kyung Hee University. This collaborative pavilion marks a significant step in Seoul’s ambition to become a startup hub, and among its participating companies, 17 received innovation awards, evidencing their excellence. The pavilion also includes 85 supporters in a significant collaboration between companies, institutions, and industry-academia cooperation.
